title: watch-rotation-sprint-notes-2026-04-12
body:
Quick summary:
- Date/shift: 2026-04-11 22:00 - 2026-04-12 06:00 PT (nightwatch rotation).
- Primary focus: investigate elevated tail latency affecting hosted API (text-generation) across us-west-2 pool.
- Outcome: degraded tail latency mitigated by rolling a config change to batch_size and enabling a temporary fallback routing policy. Root cause suspected: a combination of a model cache eviction regression (recent runtime change) + noisy KV-cache warming traffic from one tenant.

Incidents and timeline (short):
- 22:10 - Pager received: high-95th latency alerts for /v1/generate (SLO target 150ms, observed 300-1200ms). Trigger: latency-alert-queue SLO threshold. Incident labeled INC-20260411-01.
- 22:15 - Initial triage: confirmed elevated latency, spike concentrated on host shard 37 in us-west-2 serving runtime pool.
- 22:23 - Deployed interim routing rule: divert 25% of new requests from shard 37 to warm standby pool (dedicated small nodes). Immediate 30% reduction in 95th latency for served requests.
- 22:40 - Identified recurring KV cache eviction logs (OOM-ish warnings) correlated with tenant A's large prompt workflows. Noted repeated cache thrashing.
- 23:05 - Rolled back change from runtime PR 987 (kernel selection tweak) to test hypothesis that a new kernel path changed memory pressure characteristics. Observed modest improvement.
- 00:10 - Enabled temporary per-tenant throttling for Tenant A (rate-limited burst to reduce KV churn).
- 01:40 - Full mitigation: patched runtime config to lower default continuous-batch-size from 64 to 48 and increased KV-cache reserved size by 12%. Monitored for 2 hours. Metrics returned to baseline by 03:20.

Actions taken (commands / notes):
- Collected heap/KV metrics: runbook cmd `infra/metrics/collect_kv_warmth --shard=37 --window=30m` output saved to S3 key s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-20260411-01/kv-metrics-20260411-22-30.json
- Rolled routing via console: RoutePolicy: temp-divert-20260411 (25% to us-west-2-standby).
- Runtime rollback: `kubectl set image` to runtime:v2.3.4 -> runtime:v2.3.3 on shard 37 nodes (note: change was coordinated with release-engineering).
- Throttle applied via per-tenant limiter config: tenant-a.rate_limit.burst=300 -> 150

Diagnostics and evidence:
- Spike correlation table: 95th latency vs GC pauses vs KV eviction count (attached in linked_artifacts).
- Logs show a noisy client pattern from tenant A: repeated long-prefix keys causing repeated KV-cache misses.
- Post-change traces: downstream queues showed reduced queueing time; overall tail latency dropped from 900ms->140ms at the 95th.

Follow-ups and owners (short):
- Runbook updates (owner: Noah Patel) - add a short section on detecting KV thrash patterns and the quick mitigation steps (per-tenant throttling + routing diversion). Due: 2026-04-16.
- Root-cause deep dive (owner: Ava Martinez) - reproduce locally using a tenant-sim traffic generator, confirm whether kernel change + burst pattern cause eviction. Create a reproducible test in repo `sre-load-tests`. Due: 2026-04-20.
- Permanent fix for cache sizing (owner: PlatformEng team via PR) - evaluate dynamic KV reservation feature flagged in runtime roadmap. Track under SRE-4123. Due: 2026-05-01.
- Customer follow-up (owner: Customer Success lead assigned: Jonah Brooks) - notify Tenant A of observed pattern and suggest request shaping; draft email pending review. Due: 2026-04-14.

Runbook notes (draft edits):
- Insert checklist entry under "High tail latency - model serving" -> step: check KV eviction logs at /var/log/runtime/kv-evict.log and run `kv_warmth` metric tool.
- Add templated routing rule: `temp-divert-{date}` with recommended percentages (10/25/50) and rollback heuristics.
- Add a note: when rolling runtime patch/rollback, coordinate with release-engineering; expect 10-15 minute warm-up for KV caches before metrics stabilise.
- TODO: capture exact log grep commands and example outputs (I left TODO markers inline).

Communication / Slack threads:
- Created incident thread #sre-incident-inc-20260411 in channel SRE (link in linked_artifacts).
- Notified oncall@redwood and infra-ops. Escalated to PlatformEng for evaluation.

Metrics observed (brief):
- Baseline 95th pre-incident: ~140-160ms. Peak: ~1200ms. Post-mitigation: ~130-170ms.
- Error-rate: no meaningful increase in 5xx; majority were latency-only degradation.
- CPU on shard 37: average +18% vs baseline, memory pressure signs in garbage collector logs correlated with eviction events.

Outstanding questions / unresolved items:
- Did runtime kernel selection change silently alter per-request memory overhead in a way that only shows under certain prompt length distributions? (research task).
- Is Tenant A's workload something we should classify as "noisy neighbor" with explicit contract/guardrails? (CS + Legal discussion for rate-limiting in contract).
- Should we expose per-tenant KV reservation as a self-serve knob in Dedicated offering? (product discussion).

Notes to incoming shift (Maya -> next nightwatch):
- Priority 1: monitor SLO alerts for /v1/generate, keep the temp-divert policy in place until PlatformEng confirms permanent fix or we roll a runtime patch.
- Priority 2: ensure `kv_warmth` daily report runs at 03:00 PT and confirm no shrink in reserved cache across shards.
- Priority 3: follow-up with Noah for runbook PR and watch the PR for comments.
- Slack shorthand: if latency spikes >500ms 95th, trigger page and immediately divert 25% (policy exists), don't attempt wider rollback without release-eng sign-off.

Housekeeping / misc notes to self:
- I left a bunch of raw logs in /tmp/inc-20260411/ for easier local repro — will clean up after deep-dive.
- Remember to add a small blurb in the fortnightly SRE newsletter summarizing the incident learnings.

Raw TODO list (one-liners):
- [ ] Noah: runbook PR (due 2026-04-16).
- [ ] Ava: reproduce KV thrash locally (due 2026-04-20).
- [ ] PlatformEng: design permanent KV reservation strategy (epic SRE-4123).
- [ ] Jonah: draft customer note to Tenant A (due 2026-04-14).
- [ ] Maya: remove /tmp/inc-20260411 artifacts after 2026-04-20 if not needed.

Sign-off:
- Current state: mitigated, monitoring. No active customer-facing downtime detected, but follow-ups necessary.
- Incoming oncall: Liam O'Connor (please ping me on Slack if anything odd).

Notes-to-self (casual):
- "Notes to self" — keep a small checklist for quick-divert steps; we spent 8 minutes hunting where the divert UI was in the console. Make that step more discoverable.

Attachments / where artifacts are stored:
- S3 incident artifacts: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/INC-20260411-01/
- Local temp logs (do not persist): /tmp/inc-20260411/
- Runbook PR branch: git://repo/redwood/runbooks/kv-thrash-mitigation
